claims.statement: POST /api/tasks creation requires the create:task permission, title and description, enriches metadata with an advisory, hash-stamped swarm/knowledge context snapshot (Qdrant, OKF MCP, DjimitKB, episodic retrieval) appended to the description, inserts the row and the TASK_CREATED audit event in one SQLite transaction, and broadcasts task.created only after commit; retrieval failure degrades to an empty context snapshot marked degraded rather than failing creation.

Task intake treats executor-process environment and recovery provenance as server-owned: request metadata key 'environment' is rejected with EXECUTOR_ENVIRONMENT_RESERVED and all 'execution_recovery_' keys are deleted on create and stripped (with server values re-applied) on PATCH.

AuthorizationService is the task-scoped authorization authority: non-privileged users are limited by SQL visibility clause or per-task owner/created_by checks, unauthorized access to read/execute/cancel/delete returns 404 rather than 403 (non-disclosure of existence), delete is privileged-only, and canApproveForTask forbids the task owner from approving their own task.

POST /api/tasks/:id/execute requires execute:task, resolves the executor kind from request body over persisted metadata.executor over default 'opencode', rejects an in-flight task with 409 TASK_RUNNING, and delegates to ExecutionEngine.executeTask whose result distinguishes started, awaiting_approval, and denied.

ExecutionEngine.executeTask's synchronous admission chain refuses dispatch when a session or pending execution exists, the durable status is already running, metadata.execution_recovery_hold or deep_agent_assurance_hold is set, a pending execution approval exists, the assigned agent is missing/retired/unavailable or blocked by runtime governance (which cancels the task and returns denied), the owning loop run or goal is operator-paused, or skill attribution is invalid, unassigned, or ambiguous.

Before an executor runs, admitRuntime resolves the runtime at its post-boot probed version from runtime_contract_probes against the in-repo RUNTIME_ADMISSIONS ledger where a critical gate FAIL always rejects and version-pinned admissions deny on drift; every decision is persisted as an execution event, refusals are recorded as runtime_admission policy violations whether or not enforced, RUNTIME_ADMISSION_MODE=shadow records the denial while allowing the run, and every fallback attempt must re-pass admission.

CommandRiskClassifier.assessTask derives the RiskAssessment from the task row (stored risk level, review_only mode collapsing to allow, sensitive keywords escalating to HIGH and require_approval, local-opencode baseline raise, and pattern-classified requested_command with unknown commands defaulting to MEDIUM require_approval), and PolicyDecisionService.evaluate matches it against enabled approval_policies or falls back to the classifier recommendation; every assessment is persisted to risk_assessments and broadcast as risk.detected.

GovernanceGateService can only tighten a policy decision: when the executing agent/model's OpenMythos benchmark score falls below the configured floor an allow becomes require_approval (recorded as policy-decision evidence), and it never loosens a deny or approval outcome; the engine applies the same tightening again after the capacity wait.

A policy deny at admission executes nothing: the engine captures CRITICAL policy-decision evidence, persists an error event with the matching policy ids, audits execution_denied, broadcasts execution.denied_by_policy, cancels the task, and returns denied to the caller.

A require_approval verdict without a currently valid grant creates a pending approval whose metadata binds executorKind and executionInputHash, moves the task to awaiting_approval, persists an approval.requested execution event, broadcasts execution.paused_for_approval, audits execution_paused, and returns awaiting_approval; granting later drives handleApprovalDecision which records evidence, broadcasts execution.resumed_after_approval, audits execution_resumed, and re-enters executeTask.

ApprovalService owns the pending to approved/denied/expired lifecycle with a configurable TTL (APPROVAL_TTL_MS, default 1 h, clamped 5 min to 7 days); expiry is realized lazily on next read or decision and cancels a task still in awaiting_approval exactly like a denial, and decideApproval enforces that expired approvals cannot authorize execution, each approval is decided exactly once, and the requester can never be the decider (SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN).

Dispatch queues behind the global runtimeConcurrencySemaphore (RUNTIME_MAX_CONCURRENCY, default 4) and afterwards re-loads the task and revalidates everything: loop pause, agent availability, recovery/assurance holds, durable status still queued, executionInputHash equality, and a fresh risk/policy/governance evaluation recorded as queue-admission evidence; a now-deny fails with EXECUTION_POLICY_DENIED and a stale approval with EXECUTION_APPROVAL_STALE, forcing a new explicit request.

Before any external process start, startExecutionAttempt transactionally stamps provenance: an execution_events row with metadata source execution-engine phase admitted and a fresh attempt_id, plus task status running and metadata.execution_recovery_attempt pointing at that event; executor options pass server-side validation (model, reasoning effort, codex sandbox) and skipPermissions requires both metadata opt-in and RUNTIME_ALLOW_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=true.

metadata.sandbox.enabled wraps the chosen executor in DockerSandboxExecutor with configured image, CPU and memory limits, network mode and bind mounts; the deep-agent executor forbids sandboxing (the sovereign runtime owns isolation), has no fallback, and receives a contract issued in memory that is deliberately removed from durable task metadata before dispatch.

Failure handling is circuit-broken and bounded: per-executor circuit breakers (threshold default 3, recovery 30 s) gate attempts before the per-mode fallback chain (fast opencode/gemini/claude, standard claude/codex/gemini, controlled claude/codex, restricted claude only) advances up to the mode's maxRetries (1/2/3/0), a fallback must independently pass policy admission and runtime admission, and no automatic retry happens when the failure's sideEffectsPossible flag is true or it is not retryable.

Executor output is persist-before-publish: processEventStream persists each session event to execution_events then broadcasts execution.event carrying the persisted row's canonical timestamps, and the stream is truncated with a warning event after EXECUTION_EVENT_STREAM_TIMEOUT_MS (default 300 000 ms); WebSocket delivery is filtered by AuthorizationService.canReadTask against each client's rebound credentials, and the same events are readable over GET /api/tasks/:id/events.

Terminal handling releases the semaphore permit, stores metadata.executionResult and captures the post-execution repository diff (also on error) before writing completed/failed status with timestamps; completion triggers execution-summary evidence, a task.completed broadcast, and best-effort memory sync, reasoning bank, skill outcome and meta-orchestration outcome recording, while terminal transitions are audited by updateTaskStatus with user_id 'system' so engine transitions are never attributed to humans.

A completed deep-agent run never completes the task directly: the engine sets deep_agent_assurance_hold, returns the task to awaiting_approval, and records evidence that executor success is not promotion authority because the independent EVE-V assurance adapter is not installed.

cancelTask marks the session cancelled, cancels the executor, releases the semaphore permit, deletes the diff context, sets status cancelled and broadcasts task.cancelled; result handlers ignore outcomes from sessions that were cancelled or superseded (activeSessions identity check), and the cancel route refuses with 409 when the engine has no live session.

recoverInterruptedTasks runs once at server startup over durable running tasks with no live session: only when the execution_recovery_attempt stamp correlates with the latest engine-authored admitted event and both agree on mock/inProcess/not-sandboxed is the task failed as interrupted_in_process; every other case (external executors, sandboxed attempts, malformed or forged stamps, superseded mock stamps) is paused with execution_recovery_hold and outcome unknown, each transition committing an event, audit entry (automatic_replay false) and warning evidence in one transaction with no automatic replay.

The execution_recovery_hold blocks all bypasses: executeTask refuses redispatch with 409 EXECUTION_RECOVERY_REQUIRED, PATCH refuses execution-state fields while the hold is set, DELETE refuses outright, and a held task can only proceed after operator reconciliation, as pinned by task-recovery tests covering HTTP PATCH/DELETE/execute and loop-worker replay blocking.

Approval grants are input-bound: hasApprovedStart only honors the latest approval for the requested executorKind that is non-manual, status approved, unexpired, and whose metadata executionInputHash equals the hash of the current task bytes; historical approvals without the hash remain evidence but are not reusable execution grants, as pinned by the execution-approval-binding tests.

ExecutionEngine registers eleven default executors (mock, opencode, codex, claude, hermes, gemini, editor, pi, atomic, remote, and deep-agent only when DJIMIT_DEEP_ENABLED=true), and new executor kinds plug in by implementing the TaskExecutor interface and calling registerExecutor.

A task row cannot be deleted once it has an audit trail: DELETE /api/tasks/:id returns 409 TASK_HAS_AUDIT_TRAIL when any audit_events row references the task, 409 TASK_RUNNING while running, and 409 EXECUTION_RECOVERY_REQUIRED while a recovery hold is set.
